Operator:  
Good morning, and welcome to the NovaVolt Motors Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question at that time, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. If you're using a speakerphone, please pick up your handset before pressing the keys. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.  

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.  

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to NovaVolt Motors' Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Elena Vasquez, CEO; Sarah Chen, CFO; Tom Reilly, Chief Manufacturing Officer; and other members of our leadership team.  

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.  

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Elena Vasquez.  

Elena Vasquez:  
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Q3 2024 was a strong quarter for NovaVolt Motors. We made significant progress in several key areas, including substantial electric vehicle range improvements and efficiency gains that are reshaping customer perceptions and driving adoption, positive shifts in our order backlog and reservation trends signaling robust demand visibility, enhanced gross margins per vehicle through disciplined cost management, strategic capital expenditure plans focused on vertical integration, and accelerating revenue from our software and services ecosystem. The demand for our ThunderTruck continues to be strong, and we are working diligently to increase production capacity to meet that demand. The impact of our next-generation platforms is exceeding our initial expectations, with fleet-wide efficiency metrics leading the industry and positioning us for accelerated market share gains.  

Let me dive deeper into our electric vehicle range improvements and efficiency gains, which were pivotal drivers behind our impressive results this quarter. In the highly competitive EV market, range anxiety continues to be the primary obstacle to widespread adoption, cited by 42% of consumers in the latest J.D. Power APEAL study. At NovaVolt, we're not merely tackling this challenge—we're surpassing competitors with a comprehensive engineering strategy that delivers superior EPA-rated range, lower energy consumption, and enhanced real-world performance.  

Starting with the key metrics, our flagship NovaVolt S sedan, updated for model year 2025, now offers an EPA-estimated 385 miles of range on a 98 kWh usable battery pack—an 18% increase over the previous 325 miles. This is enabled by our proprietary Gen3 cylindrical cells in a 46-series format achieving 280 Wh/kg energy density, produced at our Nevada gigafactory in collaboration with top-tier cathode suppliers similar to Redwood Materials. This positions us ahead of the refreshed Tesla Model 3 Long Range at 363 miles and competitive with Lucid Air's 410 miles, all while maintaining a 25% lower MSRP.  

Our efficiency stands out even more starkly. Across our fleet, average energy consumption has improved to 228 Wh/mi, a 12% year-over-year gain and 22% better than the 2023 U.S. EV average of 292 Wh/mi according to EPA figures. Independent real-world highway tests by InsideEVs recorded our S model at 210 Wh/mi at 70 mph, attributable to an industry-leading 0.208 coefficient of drag—improved from 0.23 through active aerodynamic features like a deployable rear spoiler and CFD-optimized underbody panels. Regenerative braking efficiency has reached 75% in city driving, up from 62%, powered by advanced silicon-carbide inverters operating at 98% peak efficiency.  

These achievements stem from four core technical pillars. First, innovations in battery architecture: we've transitioned 40% of production to structural battery packs that integrate directly into the chassis, reducing weight by 15% compared to conventional pouch or prismatic designs and trimming bill-of-materials costs by $1,200 per vehicle by eliminating redundant structural elements. For entry-level models, our LFP-blended chemistry achieves 260 Wh/kg at under $60/kWh, allowing the base NovaVolt C SUV to deliver 320 EPA miles on a 75 kWh pack—more cost-effective than CATL's latest pricing.  

Second, powertrain advancements: our dual-motor AWD systems now incorporate decoupled e-axles with 92% overall efficiency, cutting drivetrain losses by 8%. Over-the-air software updates have introduced adaptive thermal management that preconditions batteries for optimal state-of-charge ranges, providing 5-7% additional range in cold weather—vital given our Q3 data showing a 14% sales softness in northern Europe below 32°F.  

Third, lightweighting and aerodynamics: employing 800 MPa advanced high-strength steel and recycled aluminum from closed-loop sources, we've reduced curb weight by 180 pounds on the S platform. Paired with vortex generators and laminar-flow tires developed alongside Michelin, this yields a 10% highway efficiency boost.  

Fourth, software-defined optimizations: NovaOS 4.0 features predictive routing powered by NREL-validated energy models, which customers report extend effective range by 8-12% on long journeys by accounting for elevation, wind, and traffic patterns.  

These enhancements are spurring regional growth. In North America, IRA-compliant builds have fueled a 35% year-over-year increase in 300+ mile models, securing 12% premium SUV segment share per Cox Automotive—surpassing Ford's Mustang Mach-E at 312 miles. In Europe, WLTP ranges over 620 km for the S outpace BMW i4's 590 km, driving 22% volume growth amid CAFE pressures; range-capable models now comprise 65% of deliveries, addressing rural charging gaps where 68% of stations remain urban per EU data. In China, our joint venture ramps 4680-equipped vans to 450 km CLTC range, maintaining 8% share versus BYD's Song L at 555 km but with 15% lower total cost of ownership thanks to superior efficiency.  

Importantly, these improvements enhance margins: cost per mile has dropped 16% to $0.028 versus Tesla's estimated $0.033, lifting EV gross margins to 24.5%—up 310 basis points quarter-over-quarter. We're on pace for 400+ mile ranges across the lineup by 2026 with solid-state cells targeting 400 Wh/kg via our QuantumScape partnership and 800V systems supporting 350 kW fast charging for 10-80% in 18 minutes. This fortifies our premium pricing as we scale to 1.2 million units yearly, differentiating from GM's Ultium platform averaging 280 Wh/mi. In essence, our range and efficiency prowess is both engineering leadership and a commercial advantage, fueling 42% gross profit growth this quarter.  

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen to discuss our financial performance in more detail.  

Sarah Chen:  
Thank you, Elena. Good morning, everyone. For Q3 2024, our revenue reached $3.2 billion, representing a 45% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin expanded to 25.8%, reflecting our ongoing efforts to improve operational efficiency. Operating expenses were $850 million, and net income stood at $450 million. We continue to maintain a healthy balance sheet with $12.5 billion in cash and cash equivalents. Our guidance for Q4 calls for revenue of $3.5 to $3.7 billion, with automotive gross margins around 27% excluding credits, and full-year deliveries approaching 500,000 units.  

As we scale our EV platform globally, gross margin per vehicle—or GMPV, our internal key performance indicator—offers the clearest view of our operational discipline amid fierce EV pricing pressures. This metric reflects gross profit per delivered unit, incorporating average selling price, material costs, labor, overhead, and regulatory credits. In Q3, GMPV hit $13,450, a 24% year-over-year rise from $10,850 and up sequentially from $12,900 in Q2. This propelled our automotive gross margin to 25.8% excluding credits—a 420 basis point expansion that outstrips Rivian's ~16% and narrows the gap to Tesla's 19.4% auto margin ex-credits. That's $13,450 in real profit per NovaVolt One sedan or ThunderTruck SUV.  

ASP remained stable at $51,200, buoyed by a richer mix: 42% ThunderTruck Long Range AWD deliveries at over $68,000 ASP, versus 28% last year, offset somewhat by entry-level One Core at $39,500 for fleet sales. Regulatory credits contributed $1,200 per vehicle on average, with $180 million recognized—up 15% year-over-year—from California ZEV mandates and European programs.  

Cost of goods sold per vehicle fell to $37,750, down 18% year-over-year. Battery costs, 35% of COGS, declined 22% to $13,200 per unit as our in-house LFP/NMC hybrid packs reached 85% localization, aided by lithium carbonate prices dropping 40% to $12,000 per ton and 92% yields at our 50 GWh Nevada cell fab—saving $2,500 versus CATL or LG outsourcing. Gen 2 ThunderTruck structural batteries target another 15% cut next year. Powertrain and electronics costs eased 25% to $4,800, with semiconductors normalized via TSMC dual-sourcing and Wolfspeed SiC partnerships; our 800V setup trims thermal costs by 12%. Manufacturing leveraged gigacasting at Austin Gigafactory—front and rear underbodies as single pieces—slashing body-in-white labor 68% and parts from 370 to 110. Utilization reached 96% at Fremont, Shanghai, and Berlin, improving overhead absorption by 300 basis points with Optimus-like bots handling 25% of assembly.  

By region: North America (65% deliveries) at $15,200 GMPV, lifted by $7,500 IRA 30D credits; ThunderTruck outsold F-150 Lightning 2:1 with 18,000 units. China (22%) at $10,800 amid BYD pressure but competitive via Shanghai's 115% utilization and LFP; Europe (13%) at $12,500 with €4,000 incentives and $220 million YTD CO2 credits, Berlin ramping to 5,000 weekly.  

Our 70% battery stack and 55% semiconductor ownership de-risks supply amid tensions, recovering from 2023's 20% price erosion as inventories normalize to 2.1 weeks. Q4 GMPV guidance is $14,200 for 27% margins, via 4680 cells (15% cheaper), 32% FSD take rate for 20% ASP lift, and Austin Phase 2 at 500k run-rate. Risks include lithium swings, 25% U.S. tariffs on Chinese cells, and Xiaomi SU7 rivalry, but our $28k cost floor supports 25%+ margins.  

Turning to capital expenditure plans and investment priorities, our FY2024 CapEx is $12.5 billion, up 25% from $10 billion in 2023, to seize share from Tesla, BYD, and legacy players like Ford and GM. CapEx intensity targets 15-18% of revenue, down from 22%, aligning with Tesla's Model 3 ramp and below Rivian's 25%+.  

Priority one, battery ecosystem at 45% or $5.6 billion: $3.2 billion expands Nevada Gigafactory 2 to 100 GWh by 2025, including $1.5 billion for 4680 dry-electrode lines cutting costs 15-20%/kWh for 500+ mile packs. $1.2 billion builds a 50 GWh LFP plant in Spartanburg, SC, for $3-4 billion IRA credits; $800 million funds Berlin JV with Northvolt to 30 GWh against EU tariffs. Silicon-anode pilots hit 350 Wh/kg.  

Priority two, vehicle production at 30% or $3.75 billion: $2.5 billion scales Oakland Lines 4/5 to 1 million units by 2026 with Giga Press 2.0 gigacasting reducing V1 SUV body costs 25%; $1 billion for Zeta platform's 800V skateboard targeting sub-$30k EVs, structural packs, and Level 3 OTA. $500 million boosts Mexico for USMCA/IRA.  

Priority three, autonomy/software at 15% or $1.9 billion: $1.2 billion for H100 compute clusters training on 10 million fleet miles quarterly for LiDAR-free vision at 99.9% edge detection; $400 million digital twins and V2G.  

Priority four, supply/charging at 10% or $1.25 billion: $800 million localizes pCAM with Umicore; $450 million for 5,000 NACS chargers with Electrify America.  

This supports 20% revenue CAGR to 2027, margins to 25%, with Gigafactory payback under 4 years.  

Next, our order backlog and reservation trends highlight demand strength. Global backlog ended at $48.2 billion, up 18% quarter-over-quarter from $40.9 billion and 42% year-over-year—285,000 vehicles at $169,000 blended ASP, growing 22% in units versus 15% deliveries to 112,000, for a 2.5x ratio. Reservations hit 420,000, flat QoQ but +12% YoY; Odyssey Max grabbed 180,000 in three months post-July beta, topping Rivian R2. Conversion dipped to 28% from pricing sensitivity at 7%+ rates.  

By model: Odyssey (55%, $26.5 billion/156k units) up 25% on 520-mile range, deliveries +30% to 62k; Thunderbolt (30%, $14.4 billion/85k) +12% despite 5% delivery dip, Texas output at 1,200/week; emerging (15%, $7.3 billion/44k) +180% reservations from fleet like UPS. North America 62% ($29.9 billion) +24% on IRA/ZEV; Europe 18% ($8.7 billion) -5% on subsidies but localized; Asia 14% ($6.7 billion) +15%; ROW 6%. Q4 backlog +10-15% expected.  

Finally, software and services revenue soared to $428 million, +162% YoY from $163 million and +28% sequentially, at 14.2% of $3.02 billion total—82% margins versus 24% hardware. Subscriptions $285 million (+185%), 1.8 million for Premium Connectivity at 62% attach/ $18.50 ARPU, 2.1% churn; Autonomy/ADAS $112 million (+210%) at 28% attach post-FSD v12.3 Level 3 cert; other $31 million. NA $278 million (+178%), Europe $94 million (+142%), China $56 million (+195%). RPO $4.8 billion. FY guidance $2.0-2.2 billion.  

I'll now turn the call over to Tom Reilly to provide an update on our manufacturing operations.  

Tom Reilly:  
Thank you, Sarah. We are pleased with the progress we've made in scaling up production of the ThunderTruck and NovaVolt One. Gigacasting and automation have driven labor reductions of over 60% in key areas, with factory utilization exceeding 95% globally. We're implementing several initiatives, including expanded 4680 cell integration and Optimus bots for assembly, to further improve efficiency and reduce costs. We are on track to meet our production targets for the year, ramping toward 2 million annual capacity by 2025 with vertical integration shielding against supply disruptions.  

Now, I'll hand the call back to the operator for the Q&A session.  

Operator:  
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one.  

Analyst 1:  
Hi, thanks for taking my question. Elena, could you expand on how the range improvements are translating to competitive positioning against Tesla and legacy OEMs in key markets?  

Elena Vasquez:  
Thanks for the question. Our 385-mile S sedan and fleet 228 Wh/mi efficiency give us a clear edge, especially at lower price points. In North America, we're gaining 12% premium SUV share over Mach-E; Europe WLTP leadership drives 22% growth; China holds via TCO. This moat supports scaling to 1.2 million units with 400-mile platforms by 2026.  

Analyst 2:  
Great, Sarah, on capex—how are you prioritizing battery investments amid lithium volatility, and what's the expected ROI?  

Sarah Chen:  
Battery scaling at $5.6 billion focuses on Nevada 100 GWh and Spartanburg LFP for IRA credits, with 4680 dry electrode for 15-20% cost cuts. ROI targets under 4 years at $100/kWh, de-risking via 85% localization against volatility.  

Analyst 3:  
Tom, can you detail manufacturing efficiencies from gigacasting and cell fab yields?  

Tom Reilly:  
Gigacasting cut body-in-white parts 70% and labor 68%, with 96% utilization. Nevada fab at 92% yields saves $2,500/pack; bots handle 25% assembly, on track for targets.  

Analyst 4:  
Elena, reservation conversion slowed—any updates on incentives to boost it?  

Elena Vasquez:  
We're addressing with 0% APR, FSD bundles, and trials targeting 40% attach. Backlog at $48.2 billion provides 2.5x visibility, Odyssey Max reservations surging 250%.  

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you for your questions. We have time for one more.  

Analyst 5:  
Sarah, impressive software growth—thoughts on ARPU expansion and RPO recognition?  

Sarah Chen:  
ARPU steady at $18.50, NA at $22; RPO $4.8 billion with 65% in 12 months. App marketplace and Level 4 push to $10 billion by 2030 at 90% margins.  

Operator:  
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Elena Vasquez for closing remarks.  

Elena Vasquez:  
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.  

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the NovaVolt Motors Q3 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.
